Jaisinghani (Chairman and Managing Director) | products = Wires and cables, electric fans, LED lighting and luminaires, switches and switchgear, solar products, conduits and accessories | revenue = {{increase}} {{INRconvert|18039|c}} (2024) | net_income = {{increase}} {{INRconvert|1802|c}} (2024){{cite news |title=Polycab India |url=https://www.indiainfoline.com/company/polycab-india-ltd/management-discussions |publisher=[[India Infoline]] |date=March 2024}} | num_employees = | parent = | subsidiaries = | website = {{URL|https://polycab.com/}} }} '''Polycab India Limited''' is an Indian [[electrical equipment]] company based in [[Mumbai]], [[India]]. The company manufactures and sells electrical products, including wires and cables, [[electric fan]]s, [[LED lighting]] and luminaires, [[switch]]es and [[switchgear]], solar products, and conduits and accessories.{{cite news |last1=Tripathi |first1=Naandika |title=Polycab India: Switching gears |url=https://www.forbesindia.com/article/work-in-progress/polycab-india-switching-gears/58615/1 |work=[[Forbes India]] |date=3 April 2020}} It also operates in the [[engineering, procurement, and construction]] (EPC) sector. In 2023, the company was ranked 161st on the [[Fortune India 500]] list in 2023, with revenues of {{INR}}14,206 crores.{{cite news |title=Fortune India 500 listing |url=https://www.fortuneindia.com/fortune-500/company/polycab-india?year=2023 |publisher=[[Fortune India]] |date=2023}} It is the largest wire and cable manufacturer in India and holds 25% to 26%{{cite news |last1=Agarwal |first1=Manvi |title=Polycab is wired for growth, but risks of a shock persist |url=https://www.livemint.com/market/mark-to-market/polycab-stock-is-wired-for-growth-but-risks-of-a-shock-persist-11715597963456.html |date=13 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240513115139/http://www.livemint.com/market/mark-to-market/polycab-stock-is-wired-for-growth-but-risks-of-a-shock-persist-11715597963456.html |archive-date=13 May 2024}} of the market share in the wires and cables sector in India.{{cite news |last1=Tripathi |first1=Naandita |title=Polycab India IT raids: All you need to know |url=https://www.forbesindia.com/article/news/polycab-india-it-raids-all-you-need-to-know/90851/1 |work=[[Forbes India]] |date=15 January 2024}} As of March 2023, the company operates 28 manufacturing units in [[Gujarat]], [[Maharashtra]], [[Karnataka]], [[Uttarakhand]], [[Tamil Nadu]], and the [[Union Territory of Daman and Diu|Union Territory of Daman]],{{cite news |last1=Joseph |first1=Lancelot |title=Polycab takes a leap forward |url=https://businessindia.co/magazine/polycab-takes-a-leap-forward |publisher=[[Business India]] |date=23 February 2023}} along with over 29 warehouses across India.{{cite news |last1=Jain |first1=Sakshi |title=I-T dept searches 50 premises of Polycab India; unaccounted cash transactions suspected |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/india/i-t-dept-seaches-50-premises-of-polycab-india-across-country-unaccounted-cash-transactions-suspected-2821935 |publisher=[[Deccan Herald]] |date=22 December 2023}} The company is included in the [[MSCI]] Standard Index,{{cite news |title=MSCI adds 9 Indian stocks, no exits |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/markets/msci-adds-9-indian-stocks-no-exits/article67534611.ece |publisher=[[Business Line]] |date=15 November 2023}} and is a constituent of the Nifty Midcap 100 Index{{cite news |title=Nifty Midcap 100 |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/indices/nifty-midcap-100 |publisher=[[Business Today (India)|Business Today]] |date=August 2024}} and the BSE 200 Index.{{cn|date=April 2025}} [[File:Auto EV Bharat 4.0, KTPO Exhibition and Convention Centre, Bangalore (2025) 110.jpg|thumb|right|Polycab India's wires and cables at display in Auto EV Bharat 4.0]] == History == The company's origins date back to 1964 with the establishment of Sind Electric Stores in [[Lohar Chawl]] by Thakurdas Jaisinghani, who had moved to [[Mumbai|Bombay]] from [[Pakistan]] after the [[Partition of India]]. This store dealt in various electrical products like fans, lighting fixtures, switches, and wires. By 1975, the company established Thakur Industries and a land was acquired from the [[Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation]] in [[Andheri]], Mumbai, for the construction of a cable and wire manufacturing facility. In 1983, the company formally entered the electrical goods manufacturing sector with the founding of Polycab Industries by Inder T. Jaisinghani and his brothers. A factory was established in [[Halol]], [[Gujarat]], for the production of PVC insulated wires and cables, copper and aluminum, and bare copper wire. In May 2008, the company entered into a joint venture with [[Nexans]], a French cable manufacturer. The joint venture, with an initial investment of $37 million, focused on the production of rubber cables for the shipbuilding, railway, and wind power industries.{{cite news |title=Polycab in JV with Nexans of France for rubber cables |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/energy/power/polycab-in-jv-with-nexans-of-france-for-rubber-cables/articleshow/3005813.cms |publisher=[[The Economic Times]] |date=3 May 2008}} In 2009, the company entered the [[engineering, procurement, and construction]] (EPC) sector, offering services covering the design, engineering, supply, execution, and commissioning of power distribution and rural electrification projects. In September 2008, the [[International Finance Corporation]], the private investment arm of the [[World Bank]], acquired a 12% stake in Polycab Wires for {{INR}}551.5 crore (US$120 million). This transaction valued the company's cable manufacturing business at ₹4,600 crore (US$1 billion).{{cite news |last1=Sinha |first1=Vivek |title=IFC to acquire 12% in Polycab for Rs 552 cr |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/indl-goods/svs/engineering/ifc-to-acquire-12-in-polycab-for-rs-552-cr/articleshow/3515439.cms?from=mdr |publisher=[[The Economic Times]] |date=23 September 2008}} In 2014, Polycab India Limited expanded its product range to include electric fans, LED lighting and luminaires, switches and switchgear, solar products, and conduits and accessories.{{cite news |title=Polycab India jumps 22% on market debut |url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/polycab-india-debuts-at-18-premium-over-issue-price/articleshow/68899797.cms |publisher=[[The Economic Times]] |date=16 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190505111007/http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/polycab-india-debuts-at-18-premium-over-issue-price/articleshow/68899797.cms?from=mdr |archive-date=5 May 2019}} In 2013, the company formed a joint venture with [[Nexans]], holding a 49% stake, to establish production facilities in Gujarat. The investment for this venture amounted to $55 million (approximately {{INR}}320 crore).{{cite news |title=French cable maker ties up with Polycab |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/french-cable-maker-ties-up-with-polycab-108022001102_1.html |publisher=[[Business Standard]] |date=5 February 2013}} In 2014, Polycab India Limited expanded its product range to include electric fans, LED lighting and luminaires, switches and switchgear, solar products, and conduits and accessories. Polycab India Limited established a 50:50 joint venture named Ryker Base with [[Trafigura]] (Singapore) in 2016 to strengthen its backward integration for copper. The company acquired full ownership in May 2020{{cite news |title=Polycab India buys 50% stake in Ryker from Trafigura |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/news-cm/polycab-india-buys-50-stake-in-ryker-from-trafigura-120050400559_1.html |publisher=[[Business Standard]] |date=4 May 2020}} and subsequently, Ryker Base was acquired by [[Hindalco Industries]], a subsidiary of the [[Aditya Birla Group]] in November 2021 for ₹323 crore.{{cite news |last1=Divekar |first1=Aditi |title=Hindalco Industries acquires Ryker Base for enterprise value of Rs 323 cr |url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/hindalco-industries-acquires-ryker-base-for-enterprise-value-of-rs-323-cr-121110301055_1.html |date=3 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211103103927/http://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/hindalco-industries-acquires-ryker-base-for-enterprise-value-of-rs-323-cr-121110301055_1.html |archive-date=3 November 2021}} == IPO == In October 2018, Polycab India filed its draft [[red herring prospectus]] (DRHP) with the [[Securities and Exchange Board of India]] for an [[initial public offering]].{{cite news |last1=Singh Dhanjal |first1=Swaraj |title=IFC-backed wires maker Polycab files for $270 million IPO |url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/3bM7d0Zg7YiKZ4Wldyn5dK/IFCbacked-wires-maker-Polycab-files-for-270-million-IPO.html |publisher=[[Livemint]] |date=31 October 2018}} The company went public in April 2019, listing on the [[National Stock Exchange of India]] and the [[Bombay Stock Exchange]]. The IPO was oversubscribed more than 52 times and raised ₹1,346 crore.{{cite news |last1=Tripathi |first1=Naandika |title=From Lohar chawl to Sewri, to $3.6 billion net worth |url=https://www.forbesindia.com/article/india-rich-list-2021/from-lohar-chawl-to-sewri-to-36-billion-net-worth-inder-jaisinghanis-journey-to-the-forbes-india-rich-list/71453/1 |work=[[Forbes India]] |date=10 November 2021}} == Finance == The wires and cables segment accounted for 88% of the company's sales, the Fast-Moving Electrical Goods (FMEG) segment contributed 7%, and the remaining 5% came from other segments, primarily the EPC business. The company has received a long-term credit rating of AA+ (Positive) from both [[CRISIL]]{{cite web |title=Rating Rationale |url=https://www.crisil.com/mnt/winshare/Ratings/RatingList/RatingDocs/PolycabIndiaLimited_August%2003,%202023_RR_324595.html |publisher=[[CRISIL]] |date=3 August 2023}} and [[Fitch Ratings|India Ratings and Research]].{{cite news |title=India Ratings Affirms Polycab India's Bank Facilities at 'IND AA+'/Positive; Off Rating Watch with Negative Implications |url=https://www.indiaratings.co.in/pressrelease/71498 |publisher=India Ratings |date=17 July 2024}} == Controversies == In December 2023, the [[Income Tax Department]] raided 50 offices of Polycab and discovered that the company had {{INR}}1,000 crore unaccounted cash sales, {{INR}}400 crore unaccounted cash payments made on its behalf by a distributor and {{INR}}100 crore non-genuine expenses.{{cite news |last1=Sampath |first1=Vineetha |title=Wires crossed: Polycab navigates uncertainty amid income tax raids |url=https://www.livemint.com/market/mark-to-market/wires-crossed-polycab-navigates-uncertainty-amid-income-tax-raids-11705225842025.html |access-date=22 November 2024 |work=Mint |date=15 January 2024}}{{cite news |title=No written communication from I-T Dept regarding outcome of Dec raid: Polycab |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/indl-goods/svs/engineering/no-written-communication-from-i-t-dept-regarding-outcome-of-dec-raid-polycab/articleshow/110001164.cms |access-date=22 November 2024 |work=The Economic Times |date=10 May 2024}} In March 2024, Polycab India's IT infrastructure was targeted by a [[ransomware]] attack attributed to the [[Lockbit]]{{cite news |last1=Tripathi |first1=Naandika |title=Polycab, Motilal Oswal, Bira91 among latest companies to be hit by ransomware attacks |url=https://www.forbesindia.com/article/news/polycab-motilal-oswal-bira91-among-latest-companies-to-be-hit-by-ransomware-attacks/92331/1# |work=[[Forbes India]] |date=29 March 2024}} group. The company subsequently reported that the incident did not have a significant impact on its core systems and operations.{{cite news |last1=Krishna |first1=Tanya |title=Polycab targeted by ransomware attack; company says core systems and operations not impacted |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/industry-polycab-targeted-by-ransomware-attack-company-says-core-systems-and-operations-not-impacted-3432321/ |publisher=[[The Financial Express (India)]] |date=21 March 2024}} == Awards and recognition == Polycab India has been listed in the [[Fortune India 500]] list for five consecutive years, from 2019 to 2023. Inder Jaisinghani, the chairman and managing director of Polycab India, and his family were ranked at #32 in [[Forbes India]]'s 2023 list of the 100 Richest Individuals, with a net worth of $6.4 billion (approximately ₹53,298 crores).{{cite news |last1=Shetty |first1=Karishma |title=Meet Inder Jaisinghani, the Indian businessman whose wealth almost doubled in 2023, making him one of India's richest people |url=https://www.gqindia.com/content/meet-inder-jaisinghani-the-indian-businessman-whose-wealth-almost-doubled-in-2023-making-him-one-of-indias-richest-people |publisher=[[GQ (Indian edition)|GQ]] |date=23 October 2023}} Jaisinghani was also featured on the Forbes India Rich List in 2022, ranking #60 with a net worth of $3.4 billion, and in 2021, ranking #57 with a net worth of $3.6 billion. The company has been awarded the title of "Superbrand" by [[Superbrands |Superbrands India]].{{cite web |title=Superbrands in India |url=https://in.superbrands.com/brands/ |publisher=[[Superbrands]]|date=2024}} The company was awarded a silver medal in the Consumer Durable category at the ET Brand Equity's 2023 Trendies Awards by ''[[The Economic Times]]''.{{cite news |title=ET Brand Equity's 2023 Trendies Awards |url=https://brandequity.economictimes.indiatimes.com/trendies-awards2023/winners-list |publisher=[[The Economic Times]] |date=2023}} In 2019, the Employer Branding Institute recognized Polycab India with a National Best Employer Brand Award.{{cite web |title=Employer Branding Award 2019 |url=https://www.employerbrandingawards.com/winners/national-best-employer-brand/eb_win19.html |publisher=Employer Branding Award |date=2019}} == References == {{reflist}} {{Nifty 200 companies}} {{commons category}} [[Category:Indian brands]] [[Category:Electrical engineering companies]] [[Category:Manufacturing companies based in Mumbai]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]] [[Category:Electrical equipment manufacturers]] [[Category:Engineering companies of India]] [[Category:1964 establishments in Maharashtra]] [[Category:2019 initial public offerings]] [[Category:Manufacturing companies established in 1964]]

Polycab India Limited is an Indian electrical equipment company based in Mumbai, India. The company manufactures and sells electrical products, including wires and cables, electric fans, LED lighting and luminaires, switches and switchgear, solar products, and conduits and accessories. It also operates in the engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) sector.
In 2023, the company was ranked 161st on the Fortune India 500 list in 2023, with revenues of ₹14,206 crores. It is the largest wire and cable manufacturer in India and holds 25% to 26% of the market share in the wires and cables sector in India. As of March 2023, the company operates 28 manufacturing units in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Uttarakhand, Tamil Nadu, and the Union Territory of Daman, along with over 29 warehouses across India. The company is included in the MSCI Standard Index, and is a constituent of the Nifty Midcap 100 Index and the BSE 200 Index.
